narrative.intro: Total federal contract obligations are $428B for FY2026 to date. Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers lead the ranked NAICS list with $42.5B in obligations. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction follows with $41.1B. Aircraft Manufacturing is third at $35.2B. Engineering Services and Facilities Support Services record $33.3B and $32.1B respectively. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) shows $29.7B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing accounts for $27.8B. Computer Systems Design Services and Ship Building and Repairing report $20.7B and $20B. Other Computer Related Services completes the top ten with $15B. The ranking reflects obligations across a mix of services, construction, and manufacturing industries, indicating where federal buying is concentrated in the current fiscal year to date.

sections.heading: Which NAICS industries lead federal contracting?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers lead federal contracting with $42.5B in obligations. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction follows at $41.1B, and Aircraft Manufacturing is third at $35.2B. The top ten also includes Engineering Services, Facilities Support Services, and Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing among others.

sections.heading: What does the ranking say about the mix of federal obligations?
sections.body: The ranking shows a mix of services, construction, and manufacturing among the largest NAICS markets. Engineering Services and Computer Systems Design Services represent services-heavy spending, while Aircraft Manufacturing and Ship Building and Repairing reflect manufacturing. Construction and specialized R&D also appear as sizable categories in the top ten.

faq.q: What are the biggest federal contracting industries?
faq.a: The biggest federal contracting industries are Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers ($42.5B), Commercial and Institutional Building Construction ($41.1B), and Aircraft Manufacturing ($35.2B). Engineering Services ($33.3B), Facilities Support Services ($32.1B), and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) ($29.7B) round out the next group. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing ($27.8B), Computer Systems Design Services ($20.7B), Ship Building and Repairing ($20B), and Other Computer Related Services ($15B) complete the top ten.
